headline: Community guidelines—how we create a supportive space for all learners
universal_truth: Good communities need shared expectations; guidelines protect everyone's experience
fun_facts: Communities with clear norms have more engagement and less conflict
Positive communities attract more contributors and better content
Most guideline violations are mistakes, not malice—correction usually works
discussion_questions: What makes an online community feel safe and welcoming?
How do you like to contribute to communities?
What behaviors would make you leave a community?

hook.script: The Commons is our community space—where learners share insights, ask questions, and contribute to the curriculum. For it to work well, we need shared expectations. Here's how we keep the space valuable for everyone.

cliff.script: Why do communities need guidelines? Can't people just be good to each other?

options.text: Shared expectations prevent misunderstandings—different people have different norms; explicit guidelines create clarity; they protect the community experience for everyone
options.response: Exactly. What seems obvious to one person isn't to another. Guidelines make expectations clear so everyone can participate confidently.
Good guidelines actually enable freedom by preventing the behaviors that drive people away...

fact1.title: Be Respectful
fact1.script: Disagreement is fine; disrespect isn't. Challenge ideas, not people. Assume good faith. Remember there's a human on the other side of every comment.

fact2.title: Stay On Topic
fact2.script: The Commons is for learning—curriculum feedback, insights, questions. Keep political and promotional content elsewhere. This focus keeps the space valuable.

fact3.title: Build Others Up
fact3.script: The best communities are constructive. Share insights generously. Help others who are struggling. Celebrate others' contributions. What you give to the community, you get back multiplied.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Communities thrive when members prioritize collective wellbeing. Be the kind of participant you'd want to encounter.

outro.script: Join the Commons with confidence. Contribute, connect, learn together. Follow these simple guidelines and you'll be a valued member of our learning community.

growTrack.title: Community Participation - Make Your First Contribution
growTrack.activity: Visit the Commons. Read a few contributions from other learners. Then make your first contribution: share an insight, answer a question, or offer encouragement. Welcome to the community.
